quotes: Open Kshana runs one scenario and tells you what it gives. Kshana Pro answers the questions a programme asks next, over the same engine and the same scenario files: which design to fly, how sure the answer is, and whether the mission meets its requirements in a form a review board can check.
Every open scenario kind runs in Pro unchanged, and an open scenario runs in Pro with no licence at all.
Every Pro number comes from runs of the open engine, so a Pro figure is as trustworthy as the open scenario kind it came from, and never more.
Anyone with open Kshana can re-run one and get the same figure.
Every Pro result is labelled MODELLED
Every figure keeps the tier the open engine gave it
A strict superset of open Kshana
No new physics
Reproducible in the free engine
Honest labels carried through

Which design should we fly?

Does the mission meet its requirements, and can we hand that over?
A free user scores one design they wrote by hand.

A Pro user states the design space (each variable a scenario setting with its allowed values), the constraints and two or three objectives, and gets the whole Pareto front: the designs that no other design beats on every objective at once.
The base scenario can be of any open kind, so the same tool designs a constellation around the Earth, the Moon or Mars, or trades a link budget.
Every design is one run of the open engine.
It has no cost model, so a variable no objective penalises drifts to the edge of its range.
Constellation studies score geometry only: no signal power, satellite health or terrain.
A free user gets one number, or a spread over random seeds.
A Pro user states how uncertain each input is and gets confidence bands, the probability of meeting a limit, and a ranking of the inputs that drive the result.
It works on any open scenario.
Inputs are ranked by Sobol' sensitivity indices or by standardised regression coefficients, and a ranking that is not reliable is flagged as such.
A long study can be stopped and resumed.
Inputs are treated as independent.
More runs narrow the sampling error, not the model error: a MODELLED kind stays MODELLED.

and programme tooling checks a programme's requirements against runs of the open engine: it imports requirements as comma-separated values (CSV), or as a documented subset of the Requirements Interchange Format (ReqIF) or of Systems Modeling Language version 2 (SysML v2) text
produces a verification cross-reference matrix (VCRM), a SysML v2 model, a change-impact report and an offline evidence pack.
It re-runs and recomputes nothing.

A trade study runs every architecture option as an unchanged open-engine scenario, ranks the options on a figure of merit read from each run's result, and writes an evidence pack that records each option's scenario hash, so any figure in it can be reproduced by re-running that scenario.

A clock twin is calibrated to a device's published Allan-deviation budget, then checked by estimating the twin's own Allan deviation with the open engine's estimator and comparing the two within a stated tolerance.
A twin of your own device needs your characterisation data and is built under contract and a non-disclosure agreement.

scope, method, results with a tier on every figure, limitations, and the exact scenario text run.
It writes an HTML report and exits with a non-zero code when a figure regresses, so a continuous-integration pipeline can stop on it.

Every result is modelled, and says so.

Did the last change make a figure we care about worse?
A free user runs a campaign and reads the result.

A Pro user names the figures that matter in a set of scenarios, says what worse means for each, and gets a pipeline that fails when a change to a scenario, a model or the engine makes one of them worse, or stops meeting its requirement.
It extends the scenario regression check.
A Monte Carlo figure is judged with statistics instead of a tolerance
a new set of random seeds is not called a regression and a doubled spread is.
Every run is appended to a history in which each record carries the hash of the one before, and a check reports whether that chain is intact.
A watch proves that a MODELLED figure stayed stable or moved; it does not prove the figure is true.
A figure with no stated direction is reported and never fails a run.

Will our signal plan interfere with GNSS, or suffer from it?
A free user checks one satellite's signal against one GNSS signal.

A Pro user tests one or more candidate signal plans, each a signal design and a constellation, against every open-service GNSS signal the engine models, with every satellite of the plan in view at once, and gets a verdict per plan and signal against a limit the study states.
Both directions are tested: the loss of C/N0 each plan causes to each GNSS signal, and the loss the GNSS signals cause to the plan.
Pro adds only the sum over the satellites in view at each cell of a worldwide grid and the ranking of the plans.
The limit and its source are inputs; no limit is built in.
The result is an upper bound: every satellite in view is taken at the maximum received power, with no power that varies with elevation and no receive-antenna pattern.
It is not a coordination filing and not a regulatory finding.
Can the team queue studies on its own network and prove what was delivered?
A free user runs one scenario at a time on one machine.
A Pro team queues studies on its own network, lets them run while no one watches, and can show afterwards exactly which result was delivered for which request.
It extends the on-premises service
Pro can run as a small
service on your own network: it reports its health, its version and the kinds it can run, and runs a scenario posted to it.
A job's identifier is the SHA-256 of the operation and the request, so the same request is the same job and is not run twice.
After a stop or a crash, every unfinished job is queued again and no finished job is run again.
Without a licence it serves the open engine only and refuses every Pro feature.
One request per connection, with no streaming: a client polls.
One licence for the whole service and one shared access token, not user management.
No cancellation, time limit, priority or retention policy.
